title: Kalguksu (Korean Knife-Cut Noodle Soup)
summary: A comforting Korean soup of hand-cut wheat noodles simmered in a savoury anchovy and kelp broth with courgette, potato and carrot.
equipment: large pot (at least 4 litres) with lid

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
dried stock anchovies, heads and dark guts removed
piece dried kelp (dashima or kombu), about 10 x 15 cm
Korean soup soy sauce or light soy sauce

steps.title: Make the noodle dough
steps.text: Mix the flour and salt, then work in the water and knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth and firm. A firm, well-developed dough is what lets the noodles hold their shape once cut and keep a pleasant chew in the soup.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Cover the dough tightly and set it aside on the worktop for 30 minutes. Resting relaxes the gluten so it rolls out thin later without springing back or shrinking.

steps.title: Simmer the stock
steps.text: Put the dried anchovies, kelp and 2 litres of cold water in the pot, bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes, lifting the kelp out after the first 10 minutes. Removing the kelp early stops the broth turning slimy and bitter, while the anchovies carry on building savoury depth.

steps.title: Strain the broth
steps.text: Strain the broth through a fine sieve back into the pot, discarding the anchovies and kelp. This leaves a clear, clean-tasting base for the vegetables and noodles to cook in.

steps.title: Roll and cut the noodles
steps.text: Roll the rested dough out on a generously floured worktop to about 2mm thick, dust it well with more flour, fold it loosely into a 3-layer stack and cut into 4-5mm strips, then shake the strips loose. The flour dusting between layers stops the strands sticking together once they're cut.

steps.title: Add potato and onion
steps.text: Bring the strained broth back to a simmer and add the potato and onion, cooking for 3 minutes until they begin to soften. Potato needs a slightly longer head start than the other vegetables since it takes longest to cook through.

steps.title: Simmer noodles and vegetables
steps.text: Shake any excess flour from the noodles and add them to the pot along with the courgette, carrot and garlic. Simmer for 6-7 minutes, teasing the strands apart with chopsticks, until the noodles are tender and the broth turns lightly cloudy and silky, a result of starch from the noodles thickening it as they cook.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Stir in the soy sauce and black pepper, tasting before adding any extra salt since the broth should already be well seasoned. Ladle into bowls and top with sliced spring onions and crumbled laver, if using.

tips: Flour the rolled dough generously before folding and cutting — unfloured layers will fuse together and the noodles will tear apart trying to separate them.
Pull the kelp out of the broth within 10 minutes; leaving it longer turns the stock slimy rather than clean-tasting.
Tease the noodles apart with chopsticks as they simmer, since fresh-cut strands are prone to clumping in the first few minutes.
Taste the broth before adding extra salt — the soy sauce and natural starch from the noodles often season it fully on their own.
storage: Kalguksu is best eaten freshly made, as the noodles keep absorbing broth and soften on standing. If you must store leftovers, keep broth and noodles together in the fridge for up to 1 day and reheat gently on the hob until piping hot (74°C), expecting a softer noodle texture; it doesn't freeze well. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
